newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador state oil firm says needs new investment.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador state oil firm says needs new investment.

text.p: The head of Ecuador's state-owned oil company Petroecuador warned Tuesday that the firm needs new investment to prevent a collapse in the country's oil production.

Petroecuador President Rafael Almeida said the company's budget would be revised to optimize the implementation of new investments. Without this, "production may collapse at a time when the country requires greater revenues to finance public works," Almeida said in a television interview.
Energy Minister Raul Baca expressed worries last week about falls in oil prices and their impact on the budget.
Petroecuador, which produces 90 percent of the country's crude output, is the main source of foreign currency for Ecuador.
Almeida, who took over as head of the firm on Monday, said the operational problems at Petroecuador started in 1994.
He said investments were necessary urgently to prevent the premature exhaustion of oil fields.
Ecuador currently produces some 380,000 barrels of oil a day, of which around 260,000 are exported, said Almeida.
